findings.finding: The opening identifies Kupzyk (2011) and gives a partial replication verdict. It states the original planning findings, pairs key published and reconstructed numbers, and closes with the three threshold shifts and the different rejection rates at the extreme setting.

The opening gives the partial verdict for the reconstructed samples. Before the planning background it states the 70/30 and two dropout losses, the ICC pattern, 51 exact thresholds and the 41-versus-40 count.
The longitudinal treatment-by-time planning question and the three power definitions let a reader understand what each comparison measures.
The four occasions, random effects, condition grid and method credits explain how the reconstruction was made. Pages 10–12 give commands and artifact routes for reproducing the reported calculations.

The packet, re-averaged final exemplary pairs and saved threshold/gap data support the signed effect pairs 1.327/1.275, 4.391/4.472, 6.409/6.443, .454/.438, .851/.778, 3.037/3.062, 8/7 and 14/13. The final pair is centered at 27, with original counts 41 and 40 out of 54 separately visible.
The saved 54 threshold comparisons give 51 exact matches. The text identifies each of the three earlier crossings, its power and its mask sensitivity.

Compared all 26 writer claim-map keys and locators to the packet and rendered paper. The paper covers the four design questions, original predictions and simulation design, initial and final comparisons, both denominator formulas, planning adjustments, the paired baseline, fitted means, null calibration and the worked software and precision examples.

findings.finding: The chapter and appendix evidence includes the generator, GLS/covariance inputs, fitted parameter means and both null settings. Row labels and route letters continue after a repeated header.

findings.location: Sections 7–9, pages 7–8, and mapped locations on pages 2–6
findings.finding: Checked all ten limitations against their mapped locations. The observed-count formula extension, realized versus averaged masks and missing source Monte Carlo variance remain explicit, as do the occluded markers, unavailable states, toy seeds and software settings, finite balanced-baseline comparison, design scope and unresolved original effective denominator.

The fixed critical value and paired comparison isolate the contribution of refitting in the balanced baseline. The paper gives the numerical effect and Monte Carlo standard error and leaves general equivalence unresolved.

The paper separates the R reconstruction and its package cross-checks from the reported SAS results. It treats the smaller effective denominator as an explanation consistent with the reported extreme-cell rates.

The title names Kupzyk (2011), and the abstract attributes the relative ranking, the largest losses at the lowest ICC, eight extra clusters and the usual empirical shortfall to the original study. The internal citation reaches the full UNL dissertation entry on page 13.

findings.location: Table 1, signed-effect, magnitude, direction and verdict columns and note
findings.finding: All eight rows show direction separately from magnitude and scientific verdict. Six magnitudes are smaller or larger for the five main losses and the ICC contrast, followed by two smaller integer effects. The note defines the sign against the relevant reference and gives 0.001 pp, 0.002 pp and 0.5 rounding tolerances. It distinguishes descriptive point estimates from equivalence and addresses Monte Carlo, mask and reading uncertainty separately.
The archived dissertation pp. 93–94 report 1.3 and 4.4 pp mean losses. The separate Ours cells show 1.27 and 4.47 pp from the matched final exemplary pairs in results/full/paired-contrasts.csv.

findings.location: Table 1, allocation, normal sizes and skewed sizes
findings.finding: The published 6.4, .45 and .85 pp means are stated on dissertation pp. 95–96 and supported by Table 1. The final exemplary rerun averages round to the separate Ours findings 6.44, .44 and .78 pp.

Dissertation p. 96 gives the lowest-ICC peak and a stated decline, while Table 1 implies a skew-size rebound from .609833 to .667333 pp. The rerun has the same peak and a .561356-to-.624767 pp skew-size rebound. The numeric columns compare the 15% dropout loss at .05 and .15, a different contrast from the skew-size rebound.
